approaches.approach_name: Event-driven framework with central event manager and event queue
approaches.description: The system is organized as an event framework with a single Event Manager and a single Event Queue that dispatches events in FIFO order.

addressed_attributes.rationale: A central event manager and queue provide the mechanism for accepting and dispatching events as the framework's core function.
A single, centralized event-processing structure keeps the framework behavior consistent and unified.

approaches.approach_name: Direct interaction between framework manager and application handlers
approaches.description: The Event Manager communicates directly with application handlers rather than through an intermediate layer.

addressed_attributes.rationale: Direct interaction between the manager and handlers supports event handling and component coordination in the framework.
Handler-level interaction supports plugging in different application-specific behaviors.

approaches.approach_name: Handler inheritance for standard and application-specific extensions
approaches.description: A base Handler component is extended by standard handlers and application-specific handlers.

addressed_attributes.rationale: Inheritance from a base handler allows new handler variants to be added while preserving a common interface and behavior.
Extending a base component is a localized way to introduce new application-specific behavior.

approaches.approach_name: Framework-contained main module and application logic
approaches.description: The Main module is part of the framework, and application logic is embedded within framework components.

addressed_attributes.rationale: Keeping the main module and application logic inside the framework keeps execution and control within one architectural boundary.
Embedding the application logic in framework components ensures the framework can execute the application's event-processing behavior.

approaches.description: The system accepts input through a command-line interface and processes events sequentially on a single processor.

addressed_attributes.rationale: CLI input, sequential processing, and idle waiting describe how the system receives and handles events at runtime.
Idle waiting until input is received indicates controlled event acceptance rather than uncontrolled processing.

evidence: evaluation_inputs.system_description describes an event framework with an Event Manager, Event Queue, and Handler components
evaluation_inputs.phase_2_architectural_context.runtime_constraints specifies FIFO dispatch, idle wait, and embedded application logic
evaluation_inputs.quantitative_model_parameters.architecture_limits specifies 1 event manager and 1 event queue

gaps.description: The evidence does not confirm whether the event-driven style is the architect's explicit intended style or only a descriptive label applied by the evaluator.
gaps.missing_evidence: A direct architecture statement naming the style or a diagram showing event publication/subscription semantics
gaps.resolution_question: Is the system explicitly intended to use an event-driven architecture style, and where is that stated?

gaps.description: The persistence, storage, and communication mechanisms beyond the event queue are not described.
gaps.missing_evidence: No evidence describes storage, databases, external communication protocols, or message transport beyond the queue
gaps.resolution_question: What persistence and communication mechanisms, if any, are part of the architecture?
